bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to public safety; amending the membership and appointing authority of the Minnesota Sentencing Guidelines Commission; designating the commissioner of corrections as a nonvoting member of the commission; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 244.09, subdivisions 1, 2.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 244.09, subdivision 1, is amended to read:

Subdivision 1.
Commission; establishment.
There is hereby established the Minnesota Sentencing Guidelines Commission which shall be comprised of voting and nonvoting members.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective the day following final enactment.

Sec. 2.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 244.09, subdivision 2, is amended to read:

Subd. 2.
Members.
(a) The Sentencing Guidelines Commission shall consist of the following voting members:
(1) the chief justice of the supreme court or a designee;
(2) one judge of the court of appeals, appointed by the chief judge of the appellate court;
(3) one district court judge appointed by the Judicial Council upon recommendation of the Minnesota District Judges Association;
(4) one public defender appointed by the governor after considering the slate of candidates submitted by the state public defender;
(5) one county attorney appointed by the governor after considering the slate of candidates submitted by the board of directors of the Minnesota County Attorneys Association;
(6) one peace officer as defined in section 626.84 who is a chief of a municipal police department appointed by the governor after considering the slate of candidates submitted by the Minnesota Chiefs of Police Association;
(7) one peace officer as defined in section 626.84 who is a county sheriff or deputy sheriff appointed by the governor after considering the slate of candidates submitted by the Minnesota Sheriffs' Association;
(8) one probation officer or supervised release officer appointed by the governor; and

(9) three public members appointed by the governor, one of whom shall be a person who has been the victim of a crime defined as a felony .

(b) When a position for a member representing the state public defender, board of directors of the Minnesota County Attorneys Association, board of directors of the Minnesota Chiefs of Police Association, or board of directors of the Minnesota Sheriffs' Association becomes vacant, the relevant entity must recommend at least two qualified representatives to the governor for appointment to the board.

(c) The commissioner of corrections or a designee shall serve as a nonvoting member of the commission.

(d) When an appointing authority selects individuals for membership on the commission, the authority shall make reasonable efforts to appoint qualified members of protected groups, as defined in section 43A.02, subdivision 33.
(e) The commission must elect one of the voting members to serve as chair of the commission.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective the day following final enactment.
